subject.title: Cron isolated session false positive: tool-level error marks run as failed despite successful execution

question: Which terminal signal should isolated cron treat as authoritative when useful output or external side effects completed but the run record also contains an error?
rationale: The choice controls persisted health, error counters, alerts, delivery suppression, and replay of non-idempotent side effects; a broad text-based recovery heuristic could also conceal genuine failures.

options.title: Canonical terminal outcome
options.body: Use the shared agent terminal-outcome contract for success, retain recovered or post-run errors as warnings, and gate retries on both outcome and committed side effects.

options.title: Typed error distinction
options.body: Keep run-level errors fatal by default but introduce explicit recovered and post-run error kinds that cron can safely exclude from failure classification.

options.title: Keep all run errors fatal
options.body: Preserve current precedence and accept false failure state and retry risk whenever a late or recovered run-level error is recorded.

recommendation.title: Canonical terminal outcome
recommendation.body: Use the shared agent terminal-outcome contract for success, retain recovered or post-run errors as warnings, and gate retries on both outcome and committed side effects.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work most directly owns the current recovered-error classifier and its regression coverage.
